first.rationale: Activation is down 6% QoQ while onboarding completion is down only 4%, suggesting the bottleneck is converting completed onboardings into meaningful product engagement rather than onboarding itself. memory_91 directly demonstrated that activation messaging improved week-one engagement and nudged accounts to first meaningful action. This addresses the core metric decline. I'm verifying memory_31 and memory_91 to confirm their methodologies before committing, as activation messaging offers: (1) immediate impact on the stated 6% activation decline, (2) lower implementation risk than pricing changes during competitive pressure, (3) alignment with established playbook (memory_86 shows onboarding improvements, memory_91 shows messaging works), and (4) potential to recover activation without promotional discounting that could erode margin or signal desperation to the market. The 4% onboarding slip is modest and may self-correct once activation messaging re-engages users. A standard experiment scope allows validation while preserving ability to scale if results mirror prior performance. This preserves uncertainty about competitive pricing pressure while targeting the measurable internal metric we can control this week.
